hunts.label: Friday, Nov 27
hunts.subtitle: The storm has blown itself out, and every squirrel in the woods skipped yesterday's breakfast.

rules.title: Friday after the storm
items: **Crow is open today** (Wednesday, Friday, and Saturday only).
**Dove is open** (Nov 7 to 28, bag 15). Snipe is open. HIP registration and a 3-shell plug are required for both.
**Ducks are open** to Nov 28, but you carry lead shells. Ducks need steel or other nontoxic shot, HIP, a federal duck stamp, and the NC waterfowl privilege. Skip ducks today.
**Hunter orange is required** (deer gun season is open to Jan 1). Your deer is done, but others are out.
No clock change before this hunt. All times are Eastern Standard Time.
rules.note: Confirm seasons and rules in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you go.

items: Overnight low near **44F**. An hourly walk-in temperature was not available.
9 am: no hourly figure. The day reaches about **56F**, cooler and drier than Thursday.
Wind: **SW 15 to 17 mph, gusts to about 29 mph**. Overnight SW 11 to 15, gusts near 24.
Sky and rain: **partly sunny**. NWS gives no rain chance. One backup page shows a chance of sprinkles. The ground is soaked from the storm.
Sunrise **6:56 am**. Legal light **6:26 am** (sunrise minus 30 minutes).
Moon: **waning gibbous, 82 percent**. Moonset **10:20 am**, so it is still up during the hunt. Moonrise 8:09 pm.
conditions.meaning: Assumption: squirrels and rabbits sat out a full day of storm, so hunger should bring a strong feed at first light, even with a bright moon. The wind builds through the morning, so the first two hours are the best. Expect squirrels low on trunks and on the ground, picking up cones and nuts the storm knocked down.
conditions.hours_note: The hourly table was out of date this run, so there is no 4 to 9 am chart. Figures above come from the daily forecast text.

in_season.tip: Hungry after the storm. Watch the ground under pines and oaks.
Pushed to dry, thick cover on high ground by the flood.
Watch for flight lines over the swamp. Sky shots north only.
Opportunity only. Doves fly hard with the wind at their tails.
No covey seen here yet. Bonus only.
Check fresh mud where the flood water is pulling back.

in_season: Ducks are open, but skip them: you carry lead, and ducks need steel shot and stamps.
Raccoon and opossum are open. Take only a sure, close shot.
Bear is closed until Dec 12. Bobcat is open but you do not hunt it.
Deer: tag filled for the season. Do not shoot a deer.

plan.title: Dry Rise Seat, then the Junction
plan.why: Thursday's planned seat, used now because the flood makes it the right spot. It is the **highest dry ground in the west half of the loop, between the loop and the main trail**, under **shorter pines and holly with no dead wood overhead**. Sit against a live trunk facing **northwest**. The SW wind carries your scent off to your right and behind you, away from what you are watching. The low sun rises behind your left shoulder and lights the trunks ahead. High ground holds the rabbits the water pushed out, and the pines there drop cones squirrels need after a day without food. Later, the Junction gives you open sky to the north for a passing crow or dove. Every shot goes between WNW and NNE.

steps.text: Leave the yard on the main trail. Red light only. Gun unloaded, orange on. Look up as you walk: note storm limbs hung in the canopy and go around them.
Reach the dry rise in the west half of the loop. Check overhead for dead wood. Sit against a live trunk facing NW. Load #4 with the plug in. Light off.
Legal light. Stay still. Scan the ground first, then trunks low to high, 20 to 40 yards out from WNW round to NNE.
Sunrise behind your left shoulder. This is the peak feeding window. Listen for cuttings dropping and claws on bark between gusts.
Unload. Still-hunt slowly north toward the swamp: 3 steps, stop, scan. Stop at the high-water line. Look for snipe on fresh mud. Shots N only.
Walk the swamp edge east to the Junction. Stand in the open with your back to a pine. Load #4. Watch the north sky for crow and dove for 20 minutes.
Unload. Walk back up the main trail. Kick the thickest dry cover beside it for rabbits. Kick, wait 30 seconds. Shots N, NE, or W only.
Unload and count shells. Walk out on the main trail, doing the land task.
Out at the yard. Clean and cool any game within the hour.

items: **In the gun: #4** (plug in). Squirrel and rabbit to 35 yards, crow to 35 yards.
**Right pocket: #7.5** for dove, snipe, a close rabbit, or a quail flush.
**Slugs: zipped in a separate pocket.** Bear defense only.
**No 00 buckshot carried.**
**Choke: Modified.** Fine for everything today.
**.22 LR (optional):** head shots on a squirrel only, with a trunk or the ground certain behind it. Never at a bird in the sky.
Pack - GRAB: gun, phone, water bottle filled, tell someone your plan and return time.
Pack - CHARGE: headlamp and spare flashlight before bed.
Pack - RESTOCK after the hunt: water, coffee or tea, nibble, nitrile gloves, .22 LR count, fatwood.
warnings: Never shoot a deer with birdshot. Not with #4, not with #7.5.
No ducks with these shells. Lead shot is illegal for waterfowl.
Check the barrel for mud before you load. Storm mud gets into a muzzle fast if you slip.

animals.name: Gray squirrel and fox squirrel
paragraphs: The most common game here. Grays work oaks, hickories, pines, and holly. A fox squirrel may show in the pines.
After a day hiding from the storm, expect them out early and hungry, often on the ground.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 at 20 to 35 yards, head and neck on a trunk squirrel.
On the ground, shoot only with dirt behind it and nothing beyond in the line.
After the shot, wait 10 minutes. Mark the fall against two trees.

details.title: Technique: windy-morning watch
steps: Wind shakes every branch, so look for movement that goes against the wind.
Watch the downwind side of trunks. Squirrels shelter there.
Look low. In wind they feed on the ground and lower limbs.

after: Tip: wind hides your sound. Move when a gust blows, freeze when it stops.
Tip: never shoot a squirrel moving against the sky. Wait for it to stop on a trunk.

animals.name: Rabbit
paragraphs: Cottontails left the flooded low ground. Look in the driest thick holly, briars, and brush on the rise and beside the main trail.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 or #7.5 at 15 to 25 yards, head and front shoulders.
Shoot only with the ground behind the rabbit.
Never shoot toward the south line or the field SE.

details.title: Technique: read the mud
steps: The storm washed away old sign. Every track you see now is fresh.
Follow rabbit tracks to the edge of cover and stop 10 yards short.
Kick the cover once, then wait 30 seconds before you move.

after: Tip: a rabbit sits with its back to the wind. Approach from downwind of the cover when you can.

animals.name: Crow
paragraphs: Crows travel over the swamp to and from roosts in the morning. After a storm they move to feed early.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to 35 yards. #7.5 inside 25 yards.
Shoot only birds over the north side, in open sky. Never toward the house or field.
Lead the bird: swing through from behind and keep the gun moving.

details.title: Technique: flight-line stand
steps: Stand still in the shadow of a pine at the Junction.
Watch which way the first crows travel. Others often follow the same line.
Keep your face down until a crow is in range. A bare face flashes.

after: Tip: crows fly low into a strong wind. Expect birds below the treetops coming from the SW.

animals.name: Dove
paragraphs: Mourning doves pass over open edges and water. A bonus here, not the plan.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 is the dove load.
With the wind behind them, doves are fast. Swing through and follow through.
Sky shots to the north only.

after: Tip: mark a downed dove against a trunk before you walk. They vanish in wet leaves.

animals.name: Snipe
paragraphs: A migratory bird of soft mud. As the flood water drops, new mud edges appear along the swamp.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5, close and fast.
Let the zig-zag flight straighten, then shoot.
Shots N only, over the swamp.

after: Tip: a raspy call as it flushes tells you it was a snipe.

animals.name: Quail (bonus)
paragraphs: Northern bobwhite. No covey has been seen here. See this week's skill for where they would live.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #7.5 in the right pocket.
Pick ONE bird. Never shoot into the whole covey.
Shoot only birds flying N, W, or E. Let south-bound birds go.

after: Tip: in wind, quail flush wild and early. Be ready at 25 yards, not 10.

animals.name: Raccoon and opossum
paragraphs: The flood pushed both to high ground and hollow trees. Fresh mud shows every track from last night.

details.title: Shot and load
steps: #4 to the head at 20 yards or less.
Approach from behind. Opossums play dead, so check before you handle.
details.note: Wear gloves. Rabies is possible in raccoons.

after: Tip: raccoon tracks show five long toes like a hand. Opossum hind tracks show a thumb pointing out.

animals.name: Bear and bobcat
paragraphs: Awareness only. Bear season is closed until Dec 12. Floods move animals, so watch the high ground. Give a bear space, talk out loud, and back away. Slugs are for defense only.

skill.title: Quail habitat and covey flush shooting
skill.principle: Quail live where three kinds of cover meet: thick brush to hide in, open weedy ground to feed in, and bare dirt to walk and dust in. No edge, no quail. A flush is a test of nerve: pick one bird.

sections.title: Read the habitat
steps: Look for edges where woods meet open ground. On this land, that means the yard edge and the field SE line (look, but never shoot that way).
Look for low, thick cover a person cannot walk through: briars, young pines, vines.
Look next to it for weedy open ground with seeds, and patches of bare dirt.
Look for sign: small round dust bowls in dirt, and small droppings in a tight circle where a covey roosted.
Tall, closed pine woods with no brush under them hold few or no quail.

sections.title: Listen for a covey
steps: Stand still at an edge at first light.
Listen for a loud, rising koi-lee call. Coveys call to each other before sunrise.
Point toward the sound and pace it. Log it with a note:.

sections.title: Shoot the flush
steps: Walk toward the cover with the gun at port arms, muzzle up.
When the covey bursts out, do not shoot at the group. The group is mostly air.
Pick ONE bird that is flying N, W, or E.
Mount, swing through the bird, fire, and keep the gun moving.
Mark where the other birds land. Singles hold tight for a second flush.

sections.title: After the shot
steps: Mark the fall against a tree or bush and walk straight to it.
Bag only what you need. Leave at least 8 birds in a covey so it survives the winter.
Unload before you cross any brush or fence.

details.title: Why the covey matters
paragraphs: Quail survive cold nights by roosting in a tight ring, tails in, heads out. A covey shot down to a few birds can freeze. Good quail hunters hunt a covey once and leave it.

skill.checkpoint: On your walk out, find the one spot on the land where thick cover, open weeds, and bare dirt come closest together. Pace it from the Junction and send a note: with what you see.

land.intro: The storm reset the woods. Every track in the mud is fresh, and the flood showed where water goes.
steps: Find the high-water line at the swamp edge: a band of floating leaves and sticks. Pace it from the Junction.
Note any trail that went under water, and where.
Count new blowdowns and hung-up limbs over the main trail and the loop. Strike any unsafe sit tree from your list.
Note fresh tracks in the new mud: squirrel, rabbit, raccoon, opossum. Note which way each heads.
Send what you find with a note: message, for example: note: water rose 40 paces south of the Junction, 2 pines down on the loop, coon tracks heading to the rise.

safety: NEVER shoot south. The house is SW and the field is SE: no-shoot directions.
Every shot today goes between WNW and NNE, with the ground or a trunk behind the animal.
Sky shots at crow and dove only to the north, over the swamp.
Gusts near 29 mph can drop limbs the storm cracked. Never sit or walk under hung-up limbs or dead trees.
The swamp edge may still be flooded. Water hides holes, stumps, and cypress knees. Unload before you cross wet ground or logs.
Hunter orange hat and vest are required (Oct 17 to Jan 1). Deer gun season is still open for other hunters.
hunts.regs: Check seasons, bag limits, and the crow, dove, and snipe rules in the current NCWRC Regulations Digest before you hunt.
hunts.gaps: The NWS forecast used was issued Wednesday afternoon. A newer update was not available. The hourly table was out of date (October data), so there are no hourly temperature, wind, cloud, or humidity figures and no hourly chart. The walk-in and 9 am temperatures are not known. NWS gives no rain chance for Friday, but one backup page shows a 43 percent chance of sprinkles.
